translations.text: Those were famous men across the earth, bold leaders of the people, quick to war, brave warriors, whenever shield and hand guarded the helmet on the battlefield, on the field of fate.
There they bound the hands of the holy man and fastened them by the fiend's craft, those men bound for hell, and with the edge of the sword they destroyed the sun [?] of his head.
There it was made known that holy God gave help, when the voice of the King of heaven was heard, wondrous beneath the clouds, the sound of the speech of the glorious Lord.
Endure the oppression of these peoples! It will not be long that the faith-breakers, sinful through their cunning craft, may torment you with bonds of torture.
Then the holy protector of all creatures, the creator of angels, departed to the kingdom of the homeland on high. He is rightly King, the steadfast ruler, in every place.
Then Matthew was greatly inspired anew. The helmet of night slipped away and quickly departed. Light came after, the sound of dawn.
"You must journey and bring peace, and travel to seek out the place where cannibals inhabit the land and hold their homeland by murderous arts.
Such is the custom of that multitude that they will not grant life to any stranger in that dwelling place, once the wicked ones in Mermedonia find a man without resources.
Now in three nights' time he must, in that nation, at the hands of the heathens in combat, through the grip of the spear send forth his spirit, eager to depart, unless you come first."

Then the holy keeper and ruler, the lord of the angels above, the guardian of the world, departed to seek his homeland, that glorious home, where the souls of the righteous may enjoy life after the body's fall.
The candle of heaven shone over the sea floods. There he met sailors, three glorious thanes, spirited men, sitting in a sea-boat ready for the journey, as if they had come over the sea.
They were in the clothing of seafarers, these men like voyagers on the sea, when in the embrace of the flood they toss in their ships over a far way on the cold water.

The high-prowed vessel, the swift sea-steed, quickly enclosed [by the waves], carried us with the flood on the whale-road, until we reached the land of these people, driven by the sea, as the wind drove us."

Then Andrew humbly answered him: "I would ask you, though I could give you few rings or treasure-honours, to bring us in your steep ship, the high horned ship, over the whale's homeland to that nation.
He is rightly King, ruler and maker of glorious majesty, the one eternal God of all creation, since he encompasses all by the power of one, heaven and earth, with holy might, the best of victories.

Then the eternal Lord answered him: "If you are thanes of him who raised up his majesty over the world, as you tell me, and you have kept what the Holy One commanded you, then I will carry you with joy over the sea-streams, as you request."
Then the bold-spirited men, famed for courage, climbed into the ship; on the sea-current each one's mind was gladdened.
Then the whale-mere was troubled and stirred up. The horn-fish played and glided through the ocean, and the grey gull, greedy for slaughter, wheeled about.
None of those who had boarded the ship with Andrew on the sea-stream thought that he would reach land alive. It was not yet known to them who was guiding the sea-floater through the water.
Then on the sea-way over the mingling waves, the holy Andrew, a thane loyal to his lord, gave thanks again to the mighty leader, when he had been fed:
"Now my thanes are afflicted, young warriors. The ocean roars, the sea pours. The sea-bottom is stirred up, deeply troubled; the company is distressed, the strength of the brave is greatly troubled."
At once the warriors, the hardy thanes, gave him an answer: they would not agree to leave their dear teacher at the ship's prow and choose the land for themselves.
The sea grew calm. The surge of the waves turned back again, the fierce rush of the ocean. Then, after the time of terror, the spirit of the holy man was gladdened.

"Royally brave warrior, I would like to learn one skill from you. Now that the King, the Creator of men, has given you glory and might, teach me how you steer the wave-floater, the sea-horse drenched with water, through the sea."
The surging flood cannot suddenly hinder any man against the Lord's will. He who binds the seas and who restrains and rebukes the dark waves holds power over life.

He who raised up the heavens and fixed them firm with his hands, who made them and upheld them, must rule the nations with justice. He filled the bright and wealthy dwelling with glory, and so the homeland of the angels was blessed through his might alone.

"So it is clear, the truth plain, known and recognized, that you are an excellent thane of the King who sits in majesty. The sea, the expanse of the ocean, at once recognized that you had the gift of the Holy Spirit."
"Near and far your name is holy, made beautiful with glory among the nations of men and made famous through your mercies."
"Truly it is clear, Saviour of souls, that you have been gracious to this youth and honoured him with gifts while young. He is wise in understanding and in speech."
"I have never met greater wisdom of mind in anyone of his age."

He gave speech to the dumb, and the deaf heard. He gladdened the hearts of the lame and of lepers, those who had long been sick in their limbs, weary, ailing and bound by torments. Throughout the towns the blind saw.
In the same way, on the earth he raised from death with a word many different men of the human race. The royally brave one also made known many wonders through the might of his power.
Before the multitude he consecrated wine from water, and he commanded it to turn into the better kind as a joy to the men.

"Now you can hear, dearest youth, how the Guardian of glory loved us in life by word and deed. Through his teaching he drew us toward that fair joy where those who seek the Lord after death may live free, blessed among the angels."
"It seems to me that out of envy they plotted malice through deep error. Men bent on harm obeyed the teachings of the devil, the hostile traitor, too eagerly."

Andrew then gave him an answer: "I tell you truly that he very often performed wonder after wonder before the leaders of the people, in the sight of men. The Lord of men also worked secretly for the good of the people, as he intended for their peace."
Andrew then gave him an answer: "Why do you question me with wondrous words, dearest lord, when through the power of wisdom you know the truth of every event?"
"I am not the only one. Every man's mind is filled with hope and his spirit is comforted, whether he is far or near, if he keeps in mind what the kinsman, the Son of God, did on earth."
"Spirits departed, eager for the journey, and sought the joys of heaven, the homeland of the angels, through the noble might."
At once Andrew gave him an answer: "Now I see truth in you yourself, an understanding of wisdom and success granted by wondrous power. Your heart within you blossoms with wisdom and bright bliss.
Now I will tell you yourself the beginning and the end, just as I always heard the word and wisdom of that prince from his own mouth in the gathering of men."
"Large crowds, a countless people, often gathered at the Lord's command, and there they listened to the teaching of the Holy One."

Then the protector of princes, the bright giver of glory, went on into another building, where many came toward him at the meeting-place, praising God: wise hall-counsellors. The glad-hearted men rejoiced continually at the coming of the city's guardian.
With mocking words, out of malice, the high priest began to sneer spitefully. He unlocked the treasure-chest of his heart and wove accusation.
So the leaders of men spoke, the glory-seeking company. They meant to hide the might of the Creator. Wickedness, endless evil, turned back to where it had arisen before.

Through many wonders in the wilderness he showed by his powers that he was the rightful king over the world, strengthened in might, ruler and maker of glorious majesty, the one eternal God of all creation.
The sinful did not take in the teaching of the Holy One, though he showed so many true signs where they could see them.
Likewise the Lord of victories saw wondrous marvels carved on the wall of the hall, the likeness of his angels, brightly adorned on both sides and beautifully made.
"Here the form of the holy ones is marked out: the thanes of glory, set down on the wall by skilled hands."
This is the same almighty God whom the fathers knew in days of old.
He granted grace to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and honoured them with riches. He first told Abraham in words the terms of his noble covenant: that the God of glory was to be born from his kin.
The event is open and plain among you. You can now see with your eyes the God of victory, the possessor of heaven."

Then he set out to travel over the border-paths, as the mighty Lord, the creator of men, had ordained for him, until he came, shining brightly, to Mamre, as the Creator had commanded him, where the bodies, the corpses of the patriarchs, had lain buried for a long time.
They were to make known to the people who had first made the all-green earth and the heaven above at the creation, and where the ruler who established that work was.
Then the guardian of the kingdom quickly commanded them to go back in peace to their blessedness a second time, to seek the joys of heaven and to enjoy them gladly for ever.
I know many more great and famous stories still of what the Son, the ruler of the heavens, did, which you could not bear or hold in your heart, wise in thought though you are."
So Andrew praised the teaching of the Holy One in songs all day long, until sleep suddenly came over him on the whale-road, near the King of heaven.
The shadows faded, dark under the clouds. Then came the blaze of fair weather, the bright light of heaven, shining over the buildings.
Then on the sand he saw his disciples, brave warriors, sleeping beside him.
"In that ship was the glory of kings, the ruler of mankind. I recognised his words, though he had hidden his appearance."

"Then eagles came flying over the surging waves, exulting in their feathers. While we slept they drew out our souls and carried them joyfully in flight through the air, glad with their cries, bright and gentle.
They loved us kindly and dwelt in praise. There was unceasing song and the movement of the heavens, a beautiful band of hosts and a company of glory.
Holy archangels, enthroned in majesty, served you. It is well for those men who are allowed to enjoy those joys."

Then the mind of the holy man was greatly gladdened in his heart after he heard his disciples' words: that God was willing to hold them worthy of so much, above all men. And the protector of warriors spoke this word:
Then at that same moment the Prince appeared visibly before his eyes, the King of every living being, in the form of a boy.
"I hold you in my protection, so that wicked enemies, fierce makers of harm, may not hurt your soul."
Then he fell to the ground; the man wise in words sought peace and asked his beloved lord:

"Arise now quickly, grasp my counsel at once, blessed man, for the bright Father will honour you with glorious gifts for ever, with skill and might. Go into the city, within the city's walls, where your brother is.
You must seek him and free the beloved man from the hatred of hostile men, together with all the people who live with him, wickedly bound in the malicious fetters of foreigners.
They cannot part you from your life through death, though you suffer blows and beatings from sinful men.
Bear that pain. Do not let the might of the heathens, the grim spear-strife, turn you aside so that you abandon God, your Lord.
When among the Jews I hung upon the gallows (the cross was raised up), a certain man let the sweat flow out of my side, blood to the ground.
I endured many miseries on earth. By that I wished, with a gracious mind, to set you an example, as will be shown in a foreign land."
Then the patient-minded man, hard in battle, was mindful. He went quickly into the city, a resolute champion, spurred on by courage, a man brave in spirit, true to the Creator,

A sudden onrush of death seized the sword-bloodied warriors. Then the holy man prayed to the merciful Father and, with the thoughts of his heart, praised on high the majesty of heaven's King, the lordship of God.

At once the door sprang open at the touch of the hand of the Holy Spirit, and the battle-brave man went in there, mindful of courage. The heathens slept, drunk with blood; they had reddened the field of death.

Likewise the holy man in that prison of harm greeted his God and asked him for aid, the Saviour for help, before his body should fall before the warlike might of the heathens. And then he led out of their bodily bonds, from that prison into the peace of the Lord, a hundred and two, counted by number,
where the brave men, faithful comrades, held council together before they parted in two directions.

He then sat down beside it. He had pure love and an eternal mind set on heaven, on the bliss of angels. From there, within the city's walls, he waited to see what deeds of battle would be granted to him.

Then, as I have heard, the townspeople quickly summoned the people together. Men came, a troop of warriors, riding on horses, proud on steeds, holding council, glorious with spears. Then the whole people was gathered together at the meeting-place.
The edge of the sword, sharp and hard in the storm of battle, marked with fiery patterns, in the hand of the foe, was to seek out life.
There lasting peace is always ready for whoever knows how to find it.

Then one warrior asked another again and again: "Let whoever has loyal counsel and wisdom in his mind not hide it! Now the time has come, an immense affliction; there is now great need for us to listen to the words of the wise."
You are hostile to God, the judge of hosts. Lo, you arrow of the devil, you only increase your misery.
That is Andrew, who contends against me with wondrous words before a multitude of men."
After those words came an immense host, false counsellors with a throng of shields, enraged. They quickly carried him out and there bound the hands of the holy man.
So the man glorious in victory was beaten all day until evening came. Pain went once more around the man's breast until the bright sun, radiant in the heavens, glided away to its setting.
The weather grew cold with hard hailstorms; likewise rime and frost, grey warriors, locked up the homeland of men, the dwellings of the people.
The blameless nobleman stayed glad at heart, mindful of courage, bold and enduring in hardship, in his afflictions through the winter-cold night.
Then a troop of men came to the dark prison, no small company, advancing greedy for slaughter with the clamour of a host.
"What did you intend, Andrew, by coming here into the power of hostile men? What is your glory, which you raised up in arrogance, when you brought low the worship of our gods?
When they recognized Christ's cross on his face, a glorious sign, they were terrified at that encounter, frightened and afraid, and took to flight.
The old enemy, hell's captive, began again as before to sing a song of harm: "What has happened to you, so brave, my warriors, my shield-companions, that you have had so little success?"
"Let us go back, so that we may mock him, bound fast in his bonds, and taunt him with his miserable exile. Have your words ready, all thought out, against that monster!"
Then he cried out in a loud voice, tormented by punishments, and spoke these words: "You, Andrew, have long carried on with your monstrous arts!"
"Who of the race of men is so mighty across the earth that he could free you from the bonds on your limbs against my will?"

Then in the hour before dawn, at daybreak, a band of heathens came with a troop of people to visit the holy man. They ordered the thegn, hardened by suffering, to be led out a third time. They wanted to break the brave man's spirit once and for all. It could not be done!
"And now for three days I have had to suffer cruel tortures. I pray, God of hosts, giver of feasts to souls, that I may give up my spirit into your own hand."
"Now my sinews are torn loose and my blood has dripped away. My locks lie scattered across the land, my hair on the ground. Death is much dearer to me than this life of sorrow."
Then, following the words of the King of glory, the beloved warrior looked behind him.
Mighty and brave-hearted, wise and wonderfully shrewd, he spoke to one of them and at once raised his voice:
"By his holy command you must quickly make it known, if you have any understanding of him."
The doomed died. The rush of battle carried off the young in the water along the salt way. That was a burden of sorrow, a bitter beer-drinking.
An angel blocked their way. He covered the city with pale flame, hot surging fire. Inside, the pounding flood was fierce. The band of men could not manage to flee from that stronghold.
The waves rose, the waters roared, sparks of fire flew, and the flood surged with waves.
A terrifying fire came into view, a harsh devastation, with a dreadful sound.
Through the tumult of the air, blasts of flame surrounded the walls, and the waters increased.
The field of victory was calm. Wherever his foot stepped, the ground stayed dry of the flood.
Then the hill split open into a terrifying cave in the earth and let the flood, the dark waves, be swallowed up there. The abyss swallowed up all the gushing, crashing water.

He sank not only the waves there but also the worst of that crowd: fourteen hostile ravagers of the people went hurtling with the wave to destruction beneath the depths of the earth. Then many of the people left behind were terrified and fearful in heart.
Then, as the holy spirit's spoken words directed, that message was spoken in thanks to almighty God, ruler of nations.

Then men gathered in a throng from far and wide across the wine-city, nobles of one mind, and their women with them. They loyally declared that they would obey, eagerly receive the bath of baptism according to the Lord's will, and abandon idol-worship and the old heathen temples.
Then baptism was raised up among the people, noble among the men. God's law was set up rightly, good order was established in the land among the citizens, and a church was consecrated.

There God's messenger appointed one man, firm in wisdom and skilled in speech, as bishop for the people in that bright city. Before the assembled host he consecrated him through his apostolic authority,
a man named Plato, for the people's need, and he firmly commanded them to follow his teaching eagerly and carry out the counsel that leads to life.
He told them what his eager mind intended: that he would leave the city of gold, the hall-joy and treasure-hoard of men, the bright ring-hall, and seek a sea-going ship at the ocean's shore.
It was a grief for the company to bear that the leader of the people would not stay with them at all any longer.
He stayed in the wine-city, the protector of warriors, in its treasure-adorned halls, for the space of seven nights.
In the same way the holy man struck at the heathen temples, drove out the worship of idols, and cast down error.
Then, exulting with joy, he began to make haste and get ready for the sea. He wished to go himself by sea-ship to Achaia a second time, where he met the parting of soul from body, a violent death.
So that for his slayer it did not turn to laughter. Instead he went on his way into the jaws of hell, and from then on, guilty and friendless, he never found any comfort.

His might and his dominion over the world are gloriously blessed, and his glory shines over all for the saints in heaven's majesty, beautiful in glory for ever and ever, eternal among the angels. That is a noble king!"
